title: Incident evidence fusion and runbook templates for multi-metric SLO incidents
author: Priya Desai
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines a standardized evidence collection and fusion process for SRE incident reviews that involve multiple SLO signals (latency, availability, quality) and cross-cutting capacity issues. It includes runbook templates for Severity-1/2/3 workflows, an evidence fusion checklist, telemetry and sampling requirements, and automation snippets to reduce manual forensics time.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood inference services that contribute to customer-facing SLOs (hosted API, Dedicated inference pools, and Private control plane). This is intended for oncall SREs, incident commanders (ICs), service owners, and post-incident reviewers.

Why we need evidence fusion
- Incidents often show correlated but distinct symptoms across metrics: tail-latency spikes in generation routes, KV cache miss cascades, and token-level timeouts in streaming payloads.
- Fragmented evidence (logs only, traces only, or token samples only) leads to long hypothesis cycles.
- A reproducible, machine-assisted fusion process reduces mean time to root cause (MTTR) and improves the quality of post-incident action items.

Definitions
- Evidence: any telemetry artifact (logs, traces, token-level samples, GPU telemetry, queue length metrics, capacity reservation/eviction events, A/B rollout flags).
- Fusion: process of aligning and correlating evidence artifacts across time, request id, tenant id, and model-version meta to build an incident hypothesis.
- Fusion key: the unique identifiers used to join artifacts (request_id, trace_id, tenant_id, model_version, cluster_id).

High-level process (summary)
1) Triage & stabilize: identify impacted SLO(s), declare severity, enable immediate fallbacks (model downgrade, degraded routing, token-priority lanes).
2) Capture ephemeral evidence: preserve in-memory token sample caches, snapshot model hot pools, export current KV cache manifests.
3) Evidence collection automation: use the incident-evidence CLI (examples below) to bulk-export correlated artifacts.
4) Fuse artifacts: run the fusion pipeline to stitch logs/traces/metrics/token-samples and produce a correlated timeline.
5) Hypothesis & validate: IC and service owner form a hypothesis, create repro jobs if needed (traffic shadowing or synthetic canary).
6) Post-incident: publish a fused-evidence package and run the postmortem template.

Evidence fusion checklist (quick reference)
- Identify primary and substitute SLOs impacted and error budget consumption at time T0.
- Capture request_id and trace_id range for T0 +/- 5 minutes.
- Lock sampling policies for the affected tenants/models (increase sampling to 100% for 10 minutes if possible).
- Snapshot autoscale and eviction events for the cluster(s).
- Preserve GPU telemetry (utilization, memory pressure, kernel failures) and quantization fallback logs.
- Export function-call and tool-calling logs for any structured outputs.

Telemetry & sampling policy (minimum requirements)
Note: these are baseline requirements; service owners may increase fidelity for sensitive tenants or high-risk launches.

| Telemetry artifact                | Minimum retention / sampling | Rationale |
|----------------------------------|------------------------------|-----------|
| Request logs (all routes)        | 7 days full, 30 days indexed  | Root cause and audit |
| Traces (distributed)             | 14 days at 100% for critical routes, 7 days 10% for others | Path-level causation |
| Token-level samples               | 72 hrs at 1% default, 10% after SLO breach | Quality regressions and latencies per-token |
| GPU metrics (per-device)         | 30 days aggregated, 7 days raw | Capacity forensics |
| KV-cache manifest snapshots      | 7 days (daily), snapshot on incident | KV miss cascades |
| Autoscale and eviction events    | 90 days indexed               | Capacity planning and billing |
| A/B rollout flags and config     | 365 days                      | Rollout causation |

(Ascii table above is the canonical telemetry baseline used by the SRE telemetry pipeline.)

Runbook templates (editable below)
- Use these templates verbatim during an incident to ensure consistent evidence capture and handoffs.

1) S1: Multi-region availability / quality failure (24x7 IC)
1.1 Immediate actions (first 0-15 minutes)
   1. Declare incident severity and IC.
   2. Post initial status to #incident-ops with ETA and activation list.
   3. Run: incident-evidence export --range "T0-10m:T0+10m" --services <service-list> --force-snapshot
   4. Enable global fallback routing: router set-policy --policy degraded-routing --parents fallback-pool
   5. If error budget for affected SLO > 45% burned in last 24h, escalate to oncall-lead and product.
1.2 Evidence collection (15-60 minutes)
   - Increase token-level sampling for affected tenants: samplingctl maintain --tenant <id> --rate 10% --duration 30m
   - Snapshot hot pool metadata: svc-hotpool dump --cluster $CLUSTER --out /tmp/hotpool-$T0.json
   - Export traces: tracectl export --ids <trace_id_range> --out fused-traces-$T0.jsonl
1.3 Stabilize & mitigation (30-120 minutes)
   - Activate canary rollback or model downgrade.
   - If capacity is constrained, run pre-agreed emergency capacity policy: capacityctl preempt --policy soft-evict --targets <noncritical-tenants>
1.4 Post-incident artifacts
   - Publish fused evidence package to incident bucket: incident-evidence package --t0 $T0 --out gs://incident-evidence/$INCIDENT_ID.zip
   - Populate the postmortem template (below) and attach fused evidence.

2) S2: Latency tail spike correlated with quantization fallback
2.1 Immediate triage
   - Identify affected model versions: modelctl list-versions --filter "quantization:enabled" --since $T0-30m
   - Run kernel-fallback-checker: kernelcheck --cluster $CLUSTER --since $T0-20m and save /tmp/kernel-$T0.log
2.2 Evidence collection
   - Export kernel/driver logs and GPU ECC events.
   - Increase trace sampling for the generation route to 100% for 20 minutes.
2.3 Recovery & validation
   - Re-route requests to pre-quantized variant or increase batch timeout to absorb kernel slowness.
   - Run synthetic tail latency canary with the same prompt distribution.

3) S3: Capacity warning crossing conservative headroom thresholds
3.1 Triage
   - Confirm headroom metrics and immediate eviction candidates.
   - Notify capacity-steward channel and compute short-term reservations.
3.2 Evidence collection
   - Export tenant priority ledger and active reservations: capacityctl ledger --out ledger-$T0.csv
   - Run token-priority sampling for affected tenants.
3.3 Local mitigation
   - Apply temporary throttles with grace periods and schedule rebalancing.

Automation snippets (examples)
- incident-evidence export --range "2026-01-15T12:00:00Z:2026-01-15T12:20:00Z" --services rw-api, embeddings-service --out /tmp/ev-001
- fusion-pipeline run --inputs /tmp/ev-001/logs.jsonl,/tmp/ev-001/traces.jsonl --key-fields request_id,trace_id,tenant_id --out /tmp/fused-$INCIDENT_ID.jsonl
- samplingctl maintain --tenant all --rate 0.05 --duration 60m

Example fused timeline (excerpt)
- 12:03:12 UTC: client request 0x9a3f enters router (router logs)
- 12:03:12.003 UTC: request routed to pool-a (trace id 0x154-a)
- 12:03:12.8 UTC: KV cache miss observed (kv-manifest snapshot shows tenant-specific TTL misconfiguration)
- 12:03:13.4 UTC: model kernel fallback to safe path (kernel logs show fallback due to convolution timeout)
- 12:03:14.0 UTC: upstream timeout returned to caller; SLO error counted

Post-incident template (fields for the postmortem)
- Incident ID: 
- Severity: 
- Time window: 
- Primary SLO(s) impacted: 
- Error budget consumed during window: 
- Fusion keys collected: (request_ids, trace_ids, tenant_ids, model_versions)
- Root cause hypothesis: 
- Supporting fused evidence artifacts (list and location): 
- Action items (owner, priority, ETA): 
- Verification plan (how we’ll confirm the fix): 

Ownership & SLAs for fused evidence packages
- Responsibility: IC collects initial evidence; Evidence Owner (rotating SRE oncall) packages and uploads fused artifacts within 48 hours of incident closure.
- SLA: fused-evidence package availability: 99% within 48 hours for S1s, 72 hours for S2s, 7 days for S3s.
- Retention: full fused packages for S1s kept 365 days; S2s 180 days; S3s 90 days unless legal/compliance flagged.

Quality & privacy considerations
- Mask PII in request payloads before long-term storage. Use the redaction rules in /security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/redaction-guidelines.
- For customer-sensitive incidents, mark fused packages confidentiality=restricted and notify Legal.

Related operational initiatives
- Integrate fusion-pipeline with the telemetry-warehouse ingestion job to enable faster queries.
- Add a test-suite for fusion tooling in CI that validates stitchability for synthetic incidents.
- Run a quarterly "fusion fire drill" to practice capturing and packaging fused evidence under 60 minutes.

How to use these templates and where to find tooling
- Tools (incident-evidence, fusion-pipeline, samplingctl, tracectl) are installed on the SRE bastion and available to oncall. See /eng-sre/operational-tooling for CLI installation and access instructions.
- For quick start: run `incident-evidence help` on the SRE bastion; templates are under /opt/sre/templates/postmortem-template.md.

Appendix: quick CLI reference
- incident-evidence export --range <start:end> --services <svc-list> --force-snapshot --out <dir>
- fusion-pipeline run --inputs <logfile>,<tracefile> --key-fields <comma-separated-keys> --out <outfile>
- samplingctl maintain --tenant <id|all> --rate <decimal> --duration <minutes>
- capacityctl ledger --out <file.csv>

Appendix: minimal evidence bundle manifest (example)
{
  "incident_id": "INC-2026-0001",
  "t0": "2026-01-15T12:03:00Z",
  "artifacts": ["logs.jsonl","traces.jsonl","token-samples.jsonl","hotpool-20260115.json","gpu-metrics.csv"]
}
